recentItems.title: Struggling to love your city? Learn its secrets | Johno Verity | TEDxLondonBusinessSchool
recentItems.description:
In early morning bicycle rides through London, filmmaker Johno Verity discovers that learning your city's hidden history transforms how you see it, and how you see yourself.  Johno Verity is a London-based content creator, filmmaker, and urban historian known for uncovering and sharing the hidden history of cities through cycling and storytelling. Often described as “London’s cycling historian,” he explores London in the early hours of the morning, revealing the social, architectural, and historical stories embedded in familiar streets, bridges, and public spaces. 

Through short-form videos and visual storytelling, Johno has built a large and engaged audience by making history accessible, informal, and deeply connected to everyday life. His work has been featured by Cycling Weekly and the BBC, where he has been recognized for presenting history in a way that is both engaging and relatable. 

Before turning his focus to urban history, Johno worked as a professional skier and filmmaker, experiences that continue to shape his visual and narrative style. His work today sits at the intersection of curiosity, creativity, and wellbeing, encouraging people to slow down, observe, and reconnect with the places they inhabit. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Painful circumstances to powerful outcomes | James Sang Lee | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
What if the circumstances that hurt us could become the source of our greatest strength? 
Four-time ISKA Self-Defense World Champion James Sang Lee shares how a traumatic childhood experience unexpectedly shaped a life of purpose. What began as a need to protect himself evolved into world championships, multiple action films, and humanitarian work through Rock Self Defense, equipping people in more than 20 countries. 
Through compelling storytelling and a live demonstration, James explores a transformative truth: painful circumstances can produce powerful outcomes—and our greatest success may ultimately be measured not by what we achieve, but by how we serve others. Best known for martial arts action, the 4x ISKA World Champion in self-defense has appeared in numerous films as an actor, stuntman, fight choreographer, and weapons consultant, including Lethal Weapon 4, Blade, and Netflix’s #1 Plane, which starred Gerard Butler. 

James has also worked on multiple documentaries as a stunt coordinator, action designer, self-defense expert, and firearms instructor, featured on the Discovery Channel, History Channel, MTV, and more.

The internationally known martial artist’s humanitarian efforts extend with Rock Self Defense in Egypt, Ukraine, Brazil, and Sri Lanka’s nationwide Stop Harassment of Women campaign, “S.H.O.W.” The appointed ISKA Youth Ambassador has taken it a step further, utilizing his influence and expertise to produce innovative initiatives that strengthen the Autism community through Dragonfly ASD and provide access to online martial arts training, Kick Punch, for the private school and homeschool communities.

Next Up, Avail Magazine, Global Unites Qatar, Student Leadership University Egypt and human trafficking film, "Let Her Go". This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Say yes to the next step | Lynn Pietig | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
In this inspiring talk, master powerlifter Lynn Pietig shares how ordinary people can accomplish extraordinary things simply by saying “YES” to every small step along the way. Breaking the mold of traditional talks, Lynn Pietig demonstrates the power of persistence in real-time by pulling three live deadlifts on stage, culminating in a historic lift 1 pound above the current world record – creating the first-ever “TEDx Fargo Unofficial World Record.”

Lynn Pietig is a world-class masters powerlifter who proves that it is never too late to chase your ultimate passion and redefine what is possible at any stage of life.

Key Takeaways:
  *Why saying “yes” to small steps unlocks extraordinary outcomes.
  *How to apply the discipline of elite training to any personal passion.
  *Proof that age is just a number when chasing your biggest goals.

#TEDx #Powerlifting #WorldRecord #PersonalGrowth #Motivation #GoalSetting
#TEDxFargo #MastersPowerlifting #DeadliftWorldRecord Pietig and her husband operate Pietig Farms, a fifth-generation farm, where they raise corn and soybeans. She owns and operates Pietig Book-Works, a tax and accounting business. Pietig also serves as treasurer for Morgan Memorial Foundation, Inc., a nursing home and assisted living facility. Pietig was elected to the AgCountry Board in 2015; her current term ends August 31, 2027. recentItems.title: To Walk Amongst the Giants | Ryan Mauk | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
My life as a storm chaser, and a father of two, and what it means to persevere.  To Walk Amongst The Giants.

Storm Chaser, Filmmaker, and Flight RN Ryan Mauk turns the most violent skies on Earth into gripping, cinematic stories. Known for racing straight into the jaws of supercells and tornadoes, he captures nature’s fury with breathtaking clarity. As the creator of The Rear Flank docuseries, Ryan delivers an unflinching look at the raw power of storms—where danger, beauty, and human determination collide. His work has been called “Netflix-worthy,” a front-row seat to chaos that few dare to face, and even fewer can capture. recentItems.title: Bakken 2.0 - Crack the code | Ron Ness | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
Ron Ness will provide an overview of North Dakota’s energy potential and technological future, particularly focusing on enhanced oil recovery (EOR) and natural gas infrastructure. There is immense opportunity in the Bakken region, estimating 3 to 7 billion barrels of additional oil recoverable through advanced EOR methods, with another 1 billion barrels possible from conventional oil fields. However, produced gas alone cannot meet future EOR demands, emphasizing the importance of utilizing CO₂ from North Dakota’s industrial sources to achieve the full recovery potential. There are planned EOR projects scheduled in North Dakota, such as multi-well and multi-zone pilots in Williams and Dunn Counties, as well as surfactant-based EOR tests. These efforts reflect a transition toward a zero-emission, technology-driven Bakken, featuring advancements like four-mile laterals, U-turn drilling, and improved wellsite efficiency and gas capture systems. Pipeline infrastructure will be covered, highlighting the WBI Energy Bakken East Project, a 455-mile natural gas pipeline designed to expand regional capacity by 1 million dekatherms per day. The project’s goal is to enhance statewide interconnections and support North Dakota’s growing regional gas demand, which is changing rapidly as the energy landscape evolves. A forward-looking vision for North Dakota’s petroleum sector will be provided, where innovation and infrastructure expansion converge to sustain production. Ron Ness is the President of the North Dakota Petroleum Council (NDPC).  Ness, with more than 25 years with the Petroleum Council and more than 36 years of career experience, under his leadership and commitment to energy development, North Dakota oil production has increased from just over 80,000 barrels of oil per day to over 1.1 million barrels of oil per day.  Ness has been instrumental in driving the state energy policy and research, including the Legacy Fund, Oil and Gas Research Council, Outdoor Heritage Fund, and the Clean Sustainable Energy Authority. 
He serves as the industry spokesperson and manages the association, which represents more than 500 companies involved in all aspects of North Dakota’s oil and gas industry.
Prior to his position with NDPC, Ness was previously the President of the North Dakota Retail and Petroleum Marketers Association. Prior to that, he spent ten years with the State of North Dakota, most of which as the Deputy Commissioner of Labor.
Ness is a Tolna, North Dakota native, a graduate of North Dakota State University in Business and Economics. He received his Master’s in Management from the University of Mary.
Ron was appointed by Governors Schafer, Hoeven, Dalrymple, Burgum, and Armstrong to the Interstate Oil and Gas Compact Commission, the Oil and Gas Research Council, the Empower North Dakota Commission, and the Governor’s Revenue Advisory Committee.
Ness serves on the Board for Sanford Health Bismarck and is the past board chair.  He is the Chairman of the Board of Directors for the North Dakota Governor’s Cup, serves on the Boards of the Domestic Energy Producers Alliance, the Council for Secure America, and serves on the Board of Regents at the University of Mary.  Ness is also a partner in a commercial real estate group.
He previously served as the Chairman of the Board of the Energy & Environmental Research Center Foundation, and Leadership North Dakota, and served on the Board of Directors for the national Mule Deer Foundation.
Ness and his wife Becky, have three adult children and enjoy working on wildlife and habitat projects on their farm and ranch properties, as well as golfing, shooting, hunting, and traveling. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why cannabis edibles shouldn't be disguised as candy | Dr. Priya Shah | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
What happens when drugs are disguised as candy? Dr. Priya Shah explores the growing epidemic of young children consuming THC-infused edibles and the consequences she sees firsthand in the pediatric emergency department. She reveals why these poisonings are predictable and preventable, and outlines practical steps parents, policymakers, and communities can take to keep children safe.

As a pediatric emergency medicine fellow at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia and Harvard Medical School graduate, Dr. Shah is a dedicated advocate for preventing childhood injuries and creating safer spaces for children to learn, grow, and play. From testifying before Philadelphia City Council to publishing in The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times, her work is helping shape conversations that directly impact the safety and well-being of children nationwide. Priya Shah, MD is a pediatric emergency medicine fellow at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP). She earned her medical degree from Harvard Medical School and completed her pediatric residency training at CHOP. Her academic interests include medical education and legislative advocacy surrounding child injury prevention. She believes all children deserve safe spaces in which they can learn, grow, and play freely. Dr. Shah has shared her injury prevention work through oral testimony at Philadelphia City Council, presentations at local and national conferences, as well as letters published in The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times. Outside of work, she loves trying out new baking recipes, traveling, and spending time outdoors with her friends and family. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Hope is a skill | Katie Kelly Dorn | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
How do we find hope when life brings us the unthinkable—something we cannot control, change, or fix? 

We may try to muscle through grief, anxiety, trauma, or heartbreak, but difficult emotions don't disappear. They often surface as anxiety, numbness, avoidance, low motivation, or the need to control. When we shut out pain, we often lose the ability to feel joy.

Katie Kelley Dorn learned this through her work as a licensed therapist and school counselor—but most profoundly as a mother of seven. Drawing on the loss of her beloved sister Ginny, welcoming Ginny's three children into her family, and helping thousands of students and families, Katie shares what she discovered when powering through—and trying to fix everything—stopped working.

Some of life's hardest realities cannot be changed. But surrender is not giving up. It is releasing our grip on what we cannot control, processing what hurts, and turning toward the next step we can take. Unconditional love gives us the safety to face our pain, while emotional skills help us move through it instead of around it.

We don't have to wait for the hard season to end before hope can begin. Hope is something we can learn, practice, and find—even in the middle of what we cannot fix.

Katie is the author of Magnolias in Winter: Finding Hope in Life's Hard Seasons, founder of EmpowerU, and a licensed therapist and school counselor. Learn more at MagnoliasInWinter.com. Katie Kelley Dorn is a school counselor, licensed mental health therapist, entrepreneur, published author, and mother of seven, with more than a decade of experience at the intersection of education, mental health, and leadership.

She has served as a K–12 school counselor and as adjunct faculty and program director at Adler Graduate School, where she aligned led data-driven initiatives to measure program effectiveness and student mental health outcomes. As CEO and co-founder of EmpowerU, Katie has developed scalable mental health skill-building solutions for schools nationwide. She has founded three companies, including two multi-million-dollar exits.

Her work is grounded in one core belief: lasting mental health improvement does not come from fixing people—it comes from teaching the skills that build resilience, agency, and lifelong capacity. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Competition without limits | Connor McGovern | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
What if competition didn't leave people out, but helped everyone discover what they're capable of?

Nine-year NFL veteran and Able Games founder Conner McGovern explores how competition and inclusion can coexist. After creating The Able Games, a fitness competition where athletes of all abilities compete side by side, McGovern saw firsthand how competition can build confidence, reveal unexpected potential, and bring people together. He takes that idea into schools through an AI-powered tool designed to help teachers create more inclusive physical education. His story offers a powerful challenge to rethink who gets to compete, and what becomes possible when everyone gets a chance to play. I am a 9 year NFL veteran that has recently retired. I am born and raised in Fargo, ND. As my NFL career was taking off I wanted to use my platform to help the community of Fargo. I had the privilege of working with the Special Olympics in college. It ignited a passion for a segment of the population that gets over looked. With the help of TNT and Kim Pladson we started Able games. This is an all inclusive fitness completion that gets chair athletes, athletes with Down Syndrome, and Crossfit Games athletes on the same floor. That has grown into ABLE in School. This is a school program that allows the schools to implement these same principles and programs into their PE courses. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Power of a Caregiver | Rachel Arterburn | TEDxUTulsa
recentItems.description:
Recalling the heartbreaking childhood moment when her brother was placed in residential care, Rachel Arterburn reflects on the deep impact of the dedicated caregivers who supported her family through his life and eventual passing. Now leading and training a team of care professionals herself, she addresses the growing crisis facing an overworked and underappreciated caregiving workforce. She outlines actionable ways society can shift its culture to properly honor, support, and respect those who step in to hold up our shared humanity. Rachel Arterburn is a speaker, community leader, and advocate for the dignity of care. She serves as the Vice President of the Vinita Area Chamber of Commerce and works in senior care as a Recruitment, Training, and Engagement Coordinator, supporting and developing professional caregivers who serve seniors and families in her region.

Based in Vinita, Oklahoma, Rachel’s perspective is deeply shaped by both her personal and professional life. She is the sister of a brother who was profoundly autistic, an experience that gave her an early and lifelong understanding of what it means to build a life around care, patience, and advocacy. That throughline has guided her work from her early years as a preschool teacher and her work in affordable community housing, to her continued involvement in community efforts centered on care, dignity, and human connection. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The power of mind transformation | Katerina Alder | TEDxUTulsa
recentItems.description:
Growing up in the Soviet Union without exposure to individuals with disabilities, Katerina Alder experienced fear and confusion when first confronted with inclusion. Her perspective completely shifted after giving birth to a daughter with Down syndrome, leading her to defy societal expectations and raise her child as a single mother. Through her personal transformation, she went on to found Amelia's Friends Foundation to build inclusive spaces, offer vital support to immigrant families, and advocate for every child's potential. Katerina Alder is an educator, nonprofit founder, and advocate for inclusion whose life journey spans continents and cultures. A first-generation immigrant from Belarus, Katerina moved to the
United States with her family in 2008 and has called Tulsa home ever since. For over 30 years, Katerina has taught English as a Second Language, supporting multilingual learners in finding their voice, confidence and discovering the power of reading and writing. She is the founder of Amelia’s Friends Foundation, a nonprofit organization dedicated to creating friendships, inclusion, and joyful experiences for children with disabilities and their families — a mission inspired by her daughter Amelia who was born with Down Syndrome. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

What truly remains when success and applause fade away?
